passage:
At 9:40 on the last night before the project deadline, Tarun opened his sent-mail folder and his stomach dropped: he had emailed Mr. Sarkar last term's file, not this one. The portal closed at ten. Load-shedding had already stopped the fan, and the room was hot and dim.
You idiot, he thought. Useless. You can't even attach a file. He typed "I'm stupid" into his notes and stared at the words.
The phone buzzed. Anand: "Bro, done?" Tarun told him.
"If I had done this, what would you say to me?" Anand asked.
Tarun paused. "That everyone does it. Send the right one now."
"So?"
Tarun attached the correct file, added a line of apology, and pressed send at 9:52.

qa.q: At what time did Tarun press send on the correct file?
What was Tarun feeling when he typed "I'm stupid"?
qa.a: He was panicking and attacking himself, calling himself an idiot and useless over one wrong attachment.

qa.q: What helped Tarun move from self-attack to action?
qa.a: Anand's question about what Tarun would say to a friend made Tarun hear his own kinder answer, and he then fixed the problem.

qa.q: How does Anand see Tarun's mistake?
qa.a: Anand treats it as something anyone could do, and Anand's question suggests Anand does not see Tarun as useless.

grounding: After a mistake a teen calls himself stupid and useless; asking what he would tell a friend softens the cruel voice and lets him fix the problem.

passage:
Dear Lavanya,
I'm writing this instead of saying it because I'd cry.
You know I forgot to upload our group project before the deadline. After Ma'am announced it in class, I went home and spent the whole evening calling myself names. Stupid. Useless. Can't be trusted with anything. I even wrote 'idiot' in the margin of my notebook, over and over.
Then I remembered last year, when you forgot your lines in the play. I told you, 'Everyone blanks. You're not your worst five minutes.' And I meant it.
So why is the voice in my head so much meaner to me than I'd ever be to you?
I tried talking to myself the way I talked to you. It felt fake at first. But then I actually made a plan: I emailed Ma'am to ask if we could submit late with a mark cut, and I set two phone reminders for next time.
Sorry I let the group down. I'm working on not being cruel to myself about it.
Hansa

qa.q: What did Hansa write in the margin of the notebook?
How was Hansa feeling that evening after the announcement?
qa.a: Hansa felt deeply ashamed and angry about the mistake, turning it into names like stupid and useless.

qa.q: What helped Hansa move from self-attack to action?
qa.a: Asking what would be said to Lavanya in the same spot, then emailing Ma'am and setting reminders.

qa.q: How might Lavanya feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Probably touched and ready to forgive, remembering Hansa's kindness when Lavanya forgot those lines in the play.

grounding: A letter from a teen who calls themself stupid after a mistake, notices the cruel voice, asks what they'd tell a friend and makes a plan.

passage: Santosh, you asked what's up with me lately. Okay. I'm your cousin Jatin, and last Saturday I reversed Papa's scooter into the neighbour's gate. Scratched both. Papa wasn't even that angry. But my head was. For three days it ran on repeat: you're so stupid, you ruin everything, you can't do one thing right. I didn't even want to go to football. Then on Tuesday Coach made me lead the drill, and when Aryan missed a pass I shouted, 'You're useless!' He looked so hurt. And I thought, wait. That's exactly what I've been saying to myself. I'd never let anyone talk to him like that. So why me? That night, when the voice started, I asked what I'd tell Aryan. It was: 'You messed up. Fix what you can. Practise.' So I apologised to Aryan, offered to help repaint the gate, and asked Papa to practise reversing with me on Sunday.

qa.q: What did Jatin reverse the scooter into?
What was Jatin feeling in the three days after the scooter accident?
qa.a: Jatin felt ashamed and full of self-contempt, with a cruel voice repeating 'you're so stupid'.

qa.q: What question helped Jatin quiet the cruel voice?
qa.a: Asking what would be said to Aryan, which led to apologising, helping repaint the gate and practising.

qa.q: How might Aryan have felt when Jatin shouted 'You're useless'?
qa.a: Hurt and small, which is what made Jatin notice the same cruelty inside.

grounding: A spoken account of a teen who attacks themself after a mistake, notices the cruel voice through hurting a teammate, and answers it with friend-like kindness.
